High-intensity statin therapy for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease is recommended for adults aged 40–75 years with LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL or individuals with diabetes and additional risk factors [ACC/AHA, 2018]. This guidance targets primary prevention in select populations with elevated cholesterol or diabetes-related risk. 

**Key criteria from the guideline**:
- LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL without secondary causes [ACC/AHA, 2018].
- Diabetic patients with additional risk factors (e.g., family history, smoking, hypertension) [ACC/AHA, 2018].

**Note**: These recommendations are part of a broader risk-stratified approach and should be reviewed in context of individual patient risk profiles, including 10-year ASCVD risk scores, comorbidities, and treatment preferences. 

For further details, refer to the full guideline: [ACC/AHA Cholesterol Management](https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000000625). 

Always confirm with a healthcare provider for personalized decision-making.
